statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal – dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The enterprise name must be stated in Vietnamese; names may contain Latin letters, Arabic numerals, and certain permitted symbols; foreign names must be transliterated into Vietnamese phonetically; the proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any registered enterprise name or protected trademark; names of state agencies, People's Armed Forces units, political parties, and public bodies may not form part of the corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Đầu tư / Investment (when used in a manner creating misleading state affiliation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Department of Planning and Investment rejects or refuses a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative complaint with the licensing authority within 30 days of rejection; if unresolved, the complaint may be escalated to the Provincial People's Committee under Law on Complaints No. 2/2011/QH13; alternatively, the applicant may initiate administrative litigation with the People's Administrative Court within one year from the rejection decision; a revised non-conflicting name may be submitted simultaneously in the same enterprise registration dossier without an additional fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional. A virtual office may be used for correspondence and administrative support, but the LLC must maintain a real, physical head office address in Viet Nam that is accessible to tax authorities and regulators; for a purely digital video-match application, a virtual office service is acceptable as a registered address only if a separate physical service and inspection point is maintained, and the Department of Planning and Investment retains discretion to reject purely virtual addresses for enhanced due diligence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high; estimated annual probability of 38-42% for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced digital social-telephony platform, with unannounced physical inspections by the Department of Planning and Investment, tax authorities, and the State Bank of Viet Nam's AML inspection team being credible within the first 12 months of incorporation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14, particularly Articles 17, 22-24, 27, 29, 30, 47-50 and 74-78; Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14, Articles 33, 36, 38 and 39; Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on enterprise registration; Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP guiding the Law on Investment; Law on Fire Prevention and Fighting 2001, as amended 2013; Law on Environmental Protection 2020 and Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Business Registration Office (Phong Dang ky kinh doanh) of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment of the city/province where the registered head office is located; electronic filing is through the National Enterprise Registration Portal at dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration (Giay de nghi dang ky doanh nghiep) as prescribed in Form 1-1 of Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP, together with the Company Charter, List of Members, List of Legal Representatives, and Investment Registration Certificate for the foreign-invested LLC.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory general minimum paid-up charter capital applies to an LLC engaged in software/data-processing services. The charter capital is fixed by the members and must be stated in the Company Charter and ERC. For a foreign-invested LLC, the charter capital corresponding to the foreign investor's contribution must be remitted through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at a State Bank of Vietnam licensed bank. The paid-in amount must be fully contributed within 90 days after issuance of the ERC; no escrow account is required for this business line unless the IRC or an addendum imposes a capital-disbursement schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: AT A MEETING of the Members of [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, a foreign-invested limited liability company to be formed under the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14, duly convened and held on [DATE] at [REGISTERED OFFICE, CITY/PROVINCE, SOCIALIST REPUBLIC OF VIETNAM]; PRESENT: [MEMBER I, MEMBER II] holding in aggregate 100% of the intended charter capital; WHEREAS the Company intends to apply for an Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate; RESOLVED: 1. The Company shall be formed with charter capital of USD [AMOUNT], and each member subscribes to the capital contribution units set opposite their names in the List of Members. Each contribution shall be paid into the Company's DICA at a licensed Vietnamese bank within 90 days after ERC issuance in compliance with Article 48 of the Law on Enterprises 2020. 2. The Company Charter presented to this meeting is adopted as the constitutive document of the Company and shall be filed with the Business Registration Office of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment. 3. The registered office of the Company shall be [FULL VIETNAMESE ADDRESS]. The General Director is authorized to execute the office lease and all subsequent notices of change of registered address. 4. The following officers are appointed and their authorities are granted: [NAME A] as Chair of the Members' Council; [NAME B] as General Director and legal representative; and [NAME C] as Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary. Any two of these officers may sign bank instructions, contracts and legal filings, while the ERC application may be signed by the legal representative. 5. The Members' Council adopts a corporate governance pack containing an internal delegation-of-authority schedule, AML/CFT policy, data-protection policy under Decree No. 13/2023/ND-CP, and a counterparty KYC template. 6. The Officers are directed to open bank accounts, engage a licensed Vietnamese certified accounting firm, obtain fire-safety certification, submit any applicable electronic information service or social-network notice to the Ministry of Information and Communications, and complete all post-incorporation registrations. This resolution was passed unanimously and shall be effective upon incorporation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation of Viet Nam (Tong Cuc Thue), Ministry of Finance. Electronic tax portal: https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn; e-invoice portal: https://hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-invested LLC is formed by obtaining an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) and an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment. Upon ERC issuance, the LLC is automatically assigned a 10-digit Tax Identification Number (Ma So Thue) by the tax authority. The LLC must then complete VAT registration and tax information registration on the GDT e-tax portal, obtain digital certificates for e-invoicing, and activate electronic tax payment. If an automatic TIN is not assigned, the LLC must file Form 01-DK-TCT with the local General Department of Taxation office within 30 days of enterprise registration. For payments to non-residents, a foreign contractor tax registration may also be required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Vietnamese LLC is a resident corporate enterprise taxed at entity level under Corporate Income Tax on worldwide income. No pass-through taxation; no default tax-exempt zone treatment unless the enterprise is separately licensed as an Export Processing Enterprise (EPE) or located in an industrial/export processing zone with specific incentives.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available. Vietnam has no check-the-box election, no partnership-classification election for LLCs, and no hybrid mismatch entity election. The LLC is irrevocably a CIT taxpayer under Vietnamese law. Only fiscal-year election and certain accounting-method elections are available; these do not alter entity-level tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Law on Value Added Tax, Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC and related implementing regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 100,000,000 annual taxable turnover is the threshold for business households and individual manufacturers to register for VAT; however, all enterprises, including LLCs, are subject to mandatory VAT registration and must register for VAT under the national tax ID upon enterprise registration, irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All Vietnamese enterprises must issue electronic invoices in XML format with a digital signature, transmit invoice data to the General Department of Taxation's e-invoice system, and obtain a 32-digit tax authority invoice code. Tax-authority-coded e-invoices must be transmitted for clearance before issuance; self-generated e-invoices without authority codes must be transmitted to the GDT no later than the end of the business day for digital verification. API integration is mandatory for larger taxpayers and supported on the GDT e-invoice portal. No physical paper stamping applies; the digital stamp/timestamp and the tax authority invoice code constitute clearance. Invoices for revenue from foreign customers qualifying as exported services must be zero-rated; domestic revenue from Vietnamese users is invoiced at 10% VAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for goods physically exported under customs supervision, goods and services supplied to export processing enterprises and non-tariff zones, and services supplied and consumed entirely outside Vietnam in accordance with Article 9 of the VAT Law and Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC. For the Video Chat Social App, subscription, virtual gift, and advertising revenue from foreign users located outside Vietnam and consumed offshore qualifies for 0% VAT provided the LLC maintains contracts, platform transaction reports, and non-cash cross-border payment evidence. Revenue from Vietnamese users is subject to the standard 10% VAT rate. Apple IAP and Paymentwall receipts must be supported by remittance records and platform statements demonstrating the foreign purchaser/consumption location, and the absence of Vietnamese consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT MT103/MT202 evidence of non-cash payment from foreign buyer
E-invoice with tax authority code or valid self-generated e-invoice for the export shipment/service
For offshore services: platform settlement report, user location logs, and evidence that the service is performed and consumed outside Vietnam
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are highly scrutinized. If the GDT determines that the goods or services did not qualify for export, the VAT is retrospectively assessed at 10% with late-payment interest at 0.03% per day. Administrative penalties range from 100% to 300% of the underdeclared VAT amount depending on tax-fraud severity. Input VAT credits previously claimed on related purchases are clawed back. In cases of fake invoices, fictitious export contracts, or under-declared foreign revenue, the taxpayer faces criminal liability for tax evasion with penalties up to 20 years' imprisonment, fines, and confiscation of assets. All supporting documentation must be retained for at least 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam maintains current-account convertibility in accordance with its IMF Article VIII obligations; payments and transfers for current international transactions, including cross-border service fees, advertising disbursements, and profit remittances, may be settled in freely usable foreign currencies through a licensed credit institution without prior central bank approval. Capital-account transactions, however, remain restricted: foreign direct investment equity contributions must be routed through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) maintained at a licensed commercial bank, and external borrowings, intercompany loans, capital redemption, divestment proceeds, and transfer of investment capital require State Bank of Vietnam registration or approval before the funds can be moved offshore. Profit remittance is classified as a current transaction but carries substantive procedural hurdles: the foreign-invested LLC must have (i) fully executed the charter-capital contribution schedule reflected in its Investment Registration Certificate, (ii) obtained a complete set of annual audited financial statements from a State Bank-approved auditing firm, (iii) settled all corporate income tax, foreign contractor tax, value added tax, and social insurance obligations, (iv) received a shareholder resolution approving the dividend or profit distribution, and (v) submitted the quarterly DICA reporting package through its principal bank. In practice, the first profit remittance may be delayed if the audited statement reveals accumulated losses, outstanding intercompany payables, or unresolved tax arrears; contraband profit distribution without audited evidence is treated as an illegal capital-outflow event and may trigger administrative penalties and suspension of the foreign investor's remittance rights.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange No. 06/2005/PL-UBTVQH11, Decree No. 70/2014/ND-CP, and State Bank of Vietnam implementing guidance for current transactions, a resident enterprise earning foreign currency from exports of goods or services must channel such proceeds exclusively through the licensed banking system. The statutory mandate vests the State Bank with authority to impose mandatory surrender ratios on export earnings; however, in current routine administration, the State Bank has calibrated the mandatory surrender ratio at zero for ordinary exporters, allowing the enterprise to retain up to 100% of service proceeds in a foreign-currency current account opened at a licensed credit institution. The binding operational requirements are: (i) export and cross-border service receipts must be credited to the enterprise's foreign-currency payment account within 15 working days of the value date; (ii) all domestic payments between residents must be settled in Vietnamese dong (VND), requiring conversion of retained foreign currency at market rates quoted by the licensed bank; (iii) outward transfer of retained export proceeds is prohibited except where supported by underlying current-transaction documentation such as import contracts, tax remittance vouchers, royalty and license agreements, or a lawful profit-remittance dossier; and (iv) the State Bank may, exceptionally, reinstate surrender requirements as an emergency macroprudential measure during balance-of-payments pressure, in which case the ratio and timeline will be fixed by an SBV circular and applied through the principal bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low as a primary corporate treasury rail; Medium only as an ancillary collection channel. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Airwallex, WorldFirst, Payoneer, and similar non-bank payment orchestrators are not 'licensed credit institutions' under the Law on Credit Institutions and cannot lawfully maintain the Direct Investment Capital Account, cannot issue SBV-recognized foreign-exchange declarations, and cannot execute the statutory current-transaction settlement chain required for a Vietnamese foreign-invested LLC. If the EMI attempts to receive the foreign investor's charter-capital injection or service-export collections, the funds would be deemed received outside the SBV-controlled banking channel and would expose the company to foreign-exchange control violations, rejection of profit-remittance dossiers, and AML/CFT sanctions. Such EMIs may lawfully participate only as non-bank payment intermediaries (for example, facilitating App Store merchant settlements) if they operate under an SBV-licensed Payment Intermediary Services arrangement or through a licensed domestic intermediary payment service provider; the definitive treasury ledger and all FX conversion must remain within the onshore licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The State Bank of Vietnam's AML/CFT framework requires licensed credit institutions to perform face-to-face identification of the legal representative and all authorized signatories before activating any corporate account. For a foreign-invested LLC, the general director (or the delegated legal representative) and each account signatory must appear physically at the principal bank branch in Viet Nam with original passports or Vietnamese identification documents, the corporate seal, the Enterprise Registration Certificate, the Investment Registration Certificate, the passport/founding documents of all ultimate beneficial owners, the board or shareholders' resolution approving account opening and signatory authority, and proof of the registered business address. Remote and fully digital account opening is not recognized for foreign-invested entities; at best, banks permit scanned pre-screening and online interview scheduling, but the statutory KYC interview, specimen-signature certification, and corporate-seal registration must be completed in-branch, normally at the bank's head office or a designated corporate-banking center in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City. Foreign directors holding valid Vietnam e-visa or work permits may open the accounts during a single physical visit; the practical alternative of a notarized power of attorney for a Vietnamese resident signatory is accepted subject to stringent verification of the POA's authenticity and the underlying board resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-velocity, small-ticket inbound collections from Apple iTunes, Google Play, and Paymentwall merchants that are inconsistent with the declared ISIC 6311 data-processing business and that lack a transparent reconciliation trail from the app marketplace to the Vietnamese bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The bank compliance team must receive: (i) executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Distribution Agreement; (ii) Paymentwall or gateway merchant agreement together with daily settlement statements showing gross billings, platform commissions, refunds, and net settlement to the Vietnamese entity; (iii) a board-approved treasury policy describing the flow of funds from end-users to the app stores, then to the local operating account; (iv) the SBV-licensed Payment Intermediary Services license of the local PSP or a written legal opinion from the FIE's counsel confirming lawful collection mechanics; and (v) a copy of the FIE's internal AML and transaction-monitoring manual suitable for a video-chat social platform, including user KYC, age-verification, and content-moderation protocols.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: complex beneficial-ownership structure involving multiple foreign intermediate holding companies in such jurisdictions as the Cayman Islands, Singapore, or offshore financial centers, making the ultimate individual owners difficult to verify and increasing the risk of sanctions exposure or politically exposed persons (PEPs).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) updated Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate naming the direct investor; (ii) a notarized ownership chain chart from the Vietnamese LLC upward to all ultimate natural-person shareholders with percentage interests; (iii) passport copies, board resolutions, and background checks for every UBO holding more than 10 percent; (iv) corporate-registry abstracts (certificate of incumbency) and good-standing certificates from each intermediate jurisdiction; (v) banker's references for the immediate foreign shareholder from its principal bank; and (vi) a negative-match confirmation against OFAC, EU, UK, and Vietnamese sanctioned-party lists prepared by the FIE's compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: round-tripping suspicion raised by rapid transfers from the DICA into the operating VND account followed by significant telegraphic transfers to foreign technology vendors for 'development services' without visible underlying contracts, work-product evidence, or tax deductions at source.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble: (i) executed and dated service-level agreements, software development agreements, cloud-hosting agreements, and license agreements matching each outward transfer; (ii) payment milestone schedules and acceptance certificates signed by the Vietnamese general director; (iii) the vendor's tax invoices and, where applicable, evidence of foreign contractor tax (FCT) withholding remitted to the Vietnamese tax authority; (iv) the monthly FX payment applications and remittance purpose declarations filed with the principal bank identifying each transaction as a current-account service payment; (v) the quarterly DICA transaction report submitted under Circular No. 02/2021/TT-NHNN; and (vi) contemporaneous board minutes approving related-party vendor engagements, together with transfer-pricing documentation demonstrating arm's-length remuneration within the approved file.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All foreign charter-capital injections must be routed through the Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) that the foreign-invested LLC maintains at a licensed commercial bank. The remitting foreign shareholder must initiate a SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for cover) wire with the beneficiary account equal to the DICA number, beneficiary name exactly matching the Vietnamese LLC legal name, and the remittance information field referencing the Enterprise Registration Certificate number, the Investment Registration Certificate number, and the foreign investor's legal name. The receiving bank will apply its internal foreign-transfer purpose code identifying 'foreign direct investment capital contribution' (góp vốn đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài); the investor must not use generic purpose codes such as 'payment for services' or 'business operations capital', as those will be rejected or reclassified as unlawful loans. The contribution must be completed within the schedule stated in the IRC; the statutory default for contribution completion is 90 days from the date of enterprise registration unless the IRC provides a longer timeline. Upon receipt, the principal bank verifies the cumulative funded amount against the registered charter capital and reports the inflow to the State Bank through the quarterly DICA reporting mechanism. Any excess remittance above the registered charter capital cannot be treated as equity and must either be returned or re-characterized through a separate foreign-loan registration under SBV rules, failing which the enterprise faces administrative fines and disallowance of the profit-remittance path.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the video-matching social app, outbound disbursements will consist primarily of payments for foreign cloud infrastructure, content-moderation services, advertising, bandwidth, software licenses, royalties, and technical consulting. The appropriate clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer from the FIE's foreign-currency payment account via the principal bank's international correspondent network. The FIE must submit for each transfer a foreign-currency payment application, the underlying contract or invoice, the tax registration reference, and evidence of contractor withholding tax where applicable; the bank will then debit the FX account and clear the MT103 through its correspondent. Commercial letters of credit (L/Cs) and documentary collections are not appropriate for intangible service transactions and should be reserved only for future equipment or hardware importation. All such current-account payments over the VND-equivalent threshold may be settled freely without pre-approval, but each payment must be recorded in the quarterly DICA/foreign-exchange declaration. Outbound remittances for royalties must be supported by a tax registration for the royalty contract; remittances for loans or capital repatriation require prior SBV registration and must be settled from the DICA, not the operating FX account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable USD/VND forward contracts concluded with an SBV-licensed credit institution, supported by an underlying current or capital transaction exposure
USD/VND currency swap agreements (principal and interest swaps) executed with a licensed commercial bank under a master foreign-exchange derivatives agreement
Onshore USD/VND foreign-exchange options, where the specific licensed bank holds SBV approval to sell derivatives to resident corporate clients
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps associated with an SBV-registered offshore loan facility, subject to the underlying loan registration and swap counterparty being an authorized credit institution

Offshore VND non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are NOT permissible for Vietnamese resident enterprises; all hedging of VND cash flows must be executed onshore as deliverable instruments through the licensed banking system

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Báo cáo tình hình hoạt động của doanh nghiệp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment via the National Business Registration Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end; if the fiscal year is the calendar year, no later than 30 March of the following year. No extension available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 10,000,000–VND 15,000,000 for late or inaccurate filing under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP; sustained non-filing and failure to operate may lead to administrative revocation of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (FS submission after statutory audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment, the provincial Tax Department, and Ministry of Finance reporting portal when applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (30 March for calendar-year LLC); audit must be completed before submission.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit financial statements: fine under Decree 41/2018/ND-CP (generally VND 5,000,000–VND 20,000,000); failure to submit audited FS for an FDI LLC is a continuing compliance violation that may be combined with tax-assessment penalties and ultimately affect enterprise registration status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax finalization return (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department / General Department of Taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the 90th day after fiscal year-end (30 March for calendar-year); transfer-pricing documentation must be available by the filing deadline if the LLC is a related-party taxpayer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP from VND 2,500,000 to VND 15,000,000; unpaid/understated CIT accrues interest at 0.03% per day; prolonged non-filing triggers enforced tax collection and invoice-control measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business license fee declaration and payment (lệ phí môn bài)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department / local tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 January of each calendar year; newly-established enterprises pay at registration or by the deadline set in the initial exemption rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.03% per day plus administrative penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; persistent non-payment is treated as tax arrears and can lead to enforced collection and invoice restriction.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all foreign-invested LLCs in Vietnam, irrespective of revenue, assets, or headcount. No minimum turnover threshold applies; the LLC must select a licensed independent audit firm before annual FS submission. Enterprises in state-owned or public-interest sectors face separate mandatory audit thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS) applied in accordance with Law on Accounting 2015 and Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; statutory financial statements are maintained and submitted in Vietnamese đồng (VND). Application of IFRS is permitted only for consolidated/management reporting under Circular 45/2020/TT-BTC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam does not require a standalone annual UBO return. Beneficial-ownership data is confirmed through the LLC’s Annual Enterprise Report, capital-contribution/shareholder register, and AML-CDD records maintained by financial intermediaries. Any transfer of capital contribution or ownership must be notified to the business registration authority within 30 days and recorded in the statutory registers, but no separate annual UBO filing is made to the company registry.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard headline CIT rate is 20%. A preferential 10% rate for 15 years, combined with a 2-year CIT holiday and 50% reduction for the next 4 years, is available for certified software production, high-technology, and research-and-development projects under Decree 218/2013/ND-CP, Decree 71/2007/ND-CP definitions of software products, and Law on High Technology 2008. A video matching/chat social app (ISIC 6311 data processing and hosting) will qualify for software-production incentives only if the competent authority certifies the product as software and income is derived substantially from software sales or licensing; income from platform commissions, virtual gifts, and advertising generally falls outside software-production incentives and is taxable at 20%. New investment projects in industrial parks, export processing zones, and designated economically disadvantaged areas may qualify for the 2-year exemption plus 4-year 50% reduction under Article 16 of the CIT Law, but purely digital cross-border enterprises without physical investment face statutory bars to these territorial incentives. The Global Minimum Tax regime (Decree 89/2024/ND-CP) shall apply from fiscal year 2024 to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million, potentially eliminating preferential rates for constituent entities in Vietnam.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quarterly provisional CIT return: Form 02/QI-TNDN (Tờ khai thuế thu nhập doanh nghiệp tạm tính); annual CIT finalization return: Form 02/QTT-TNDN (Tờ khai quyết toán thuế thu nhập doanh nghiệp), accompanied by relevant schedules (e.g. 03-1A, 03-2A, 04). All filings are submitted electronically through the General Department of Taxation's e-Tax portal at https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn using the enterprise tax code (MST).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional tax payments with mandatory annual finalization
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT return and payment must be submitted no later than the 30th day after the end of each calendar quarter; the annual CIT finalization return must be filed no later than the 90th day after the end of the fiscal year (i.e., by 31 March for a calendar-year taxpayer). The aggregate of quarterly provisional payments must reach at least 80% of the final annual CIT liability; any shortfall below this 80% threshold triggers a 0.03% per-day interest charge on the difference between the required minimum provisional payment and the amount actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: enterprise tax code, fiscal year, company name, address, legal representative, and the box declaring whether this is a provisional or finalization filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-invested LLC, the resident enterprise tax code is used exclusively; the form is not used for the foreign investor. Any revenue attributable to a Vietnamese permanent establishment of a non-resident parent would require a separate filing under the Foreign Contractor Tax regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross turnover from all Vietnam-source and worldwide business activities, including subscription fees, video chat credits, virtual gift monetization, in-app purchases, advertising revenue, and any app store settlement proceeds from Apple IAP or Paymentwall before commission deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the full gross consideration attributable to the Vietnamese LLC, not merely the net amount remitted by the app store. Revenue is recognized on an accrual basis under Circular 78/2014/TT-BTC Article 24; unsettled store proceeds remain assessable when earned.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable business deductions supported by compliant invoices and vouchers: cost of content moderation, hosting fees, payment gateway commissions, employee salaries, marketing, and allocated overhead. Deductions are disallowed if: no actual transaction, invoice non-compliant, or charge exceeding reasonable commercial bounds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenditure paid to offshore service providers (marketing agencies, licensing platforms, content moderators) is subject to the Vietnam Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) withholding obligations; gross-up provisions apply and only the net-of-FCT amount is deductible. Payments without valid FCT withholding are disallowed. The 10% statutory cap for unrecognized cash expenditures applies to uncertified deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line C1 (Taxable income – Thu nhập chịu thuế)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income equals revenue minus deductible expenses plus other taxable receipts (e.g., foreign exchange gains, interest income, penalties received, and unexpected gains) minus the tax loss carried forward. Tax losses are available exclusively to the same taxpayer (no group relief) and can be utilized for a maximum of 5 consecutive years from the year following the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC is taxed on worldwide income as a Vietnam tax resident. Foreign-source income must be included and may qualify for a foreign tax credit under applicable Double Tax Agreements only upon full disclosure and submission of the foreign tax assessment to the Vietnamese tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line D1 (Applicable tax rate – Thuế suất)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter 20% for standard taxation, or the preferential rate (e.g., 10%, 15%) where the relevant investment certificate or competent authority decision confirms eligibility. The rate is applied to taxable income with no automatic territorial apportionment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Preferential rates cannot be applied to non-certified digital or passive income. A foreign-invested LLC engaged predominantly in cross-border video matching services without a licensed high-tech or software-production certificate must use 20%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line E1 / F1 (CIT payable – Thuế TNDN phải nộp)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT liability = taxable income × applicable rate minus tax credits, foreign tax credits, and the sum of quarterly provisional payments already made. The difference is payable upon filing the annual finalization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quarterly provisional payments must not be less than 80% of the final liability; shortfalls accrue 0.03% per-day interest from the statutory provisional deadline. If the company has overpaid, the excess is offset or refunded under Tax Administration Law 38/2019.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP ranging from a formal warning for a 1–5 day delay to VND 16 million for organizations that fail to file within 90 days after the statutory deadline. Under-declaration that results in tax shortfall attracts a penalty of 20% of the shortfall amount; tax evasion through false declarations attracts an administrative penalty of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax. Late payment interest is 0.03% per day of the unpaid tax balance, computed continuously from the statutory due date. Criminal prosecution under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015 (amended 2017) applies for deliberate evasion: fines up to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment up to 7 years for managing individuals, and for legal entities fines up to VND 20 billion, suspension of operations, or prohibition of specific business activities.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Vietnam does not impose a separate withholding tax on dividend distributions made by a Vietnamese company to its foreign shareholders. After finalization of CIT and approval of the annual financial statements, after-tax profits can be repatriated freely through the corporate bank account without additional dividend withholding. The only prerequisite is compliance with the Law on Enterprises 2020: dividends are payable only from accumulated after-tax profits, the company must remain solvent after distribution, and the shareholder resolution plus supporting audited financial statements must be maintained. The foreign investor remains subject to any home-country tax on the dividend, offset only where a relevant DTA provision or unilateral foreign tax credit exists.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For cross-border payments eligible for reduced rates under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the Vietnamese resident payer must apply the FCT withholding as a withholding agent. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident payee must submit, before or upon payment: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the DTA counterparty; (ii) a treaty relief application using the prescribed form (the form is filed through the local tax office or the Large Taxpayer Office, commonly processed under Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC); (iii) evidence of beneficial ownership, demonstrating that the payee is not a mere conduit; (iv) a written confirmation that the payee has no permanent establishment in Vietnam to which the income is effectively connected; and (v) where the payee is a corporate entity, constituent documents and proof of substantive business activity. Upon acceptance, tax authorities issue a confirmation and instruct the payer to apply the treaty rate. The Principal Purpose Test (PPT) under the Multilateral Instrument and applicable DTAs disallows treaty benefits where obtaining the benefit was a principal purpose of the arrangement; the burden of proving entitlement rests on the taxpayer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Under the Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) regime (Law on Tax Administration 38/2019, Decree 126/2020/ND-CP, Circular 80/2021/TT-BTC): (a) royalties for intellectual property, software licensing, and technical know-how are subject to deemed CIT of 10% and deemed VAT of 5% on the royalty gross amount, producing a combined effective FCT of 15% if VAT is applicable and the payer is not entitled to input VAT credit, or effectively 10% if the deemed VAT is creditable; (b) interest paid to a non-resident lender on offshore loans is subject to deemed CIT of 5%, with VAT exempt (0%), for an effective FCT rate of 5% on gross interest; no FCT applies to principal repayments. Under most Vietnamese DTAs (e.g., with China, South Korea, Japan, Singapore, and ASEAN states), royalties and interest are typically reduced to 5%–10%, usually 10% for royalties and 10% for interest, but each treaty must be inspected for the specific article, limitation-of-benefits, and the interest recipient's status as a financial institution (some treaties reduce to 10% for non-banks and 5%–7% for recognized banks). Treaty relief through the protocol above is mandatory before a reduced rate can be applied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Vietnam (VND) – Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP and Circular 09/2021/TT-BTC: (i) Local File is mandatory when the total value of controlled (related-party) transactions during the fiscal year exceeds VND 30 billion; (ii) Master File is mandatory when the taxpayer's total annual revenue exceeds VND 50 billion or the total value of controlled transactions exceeds VND 30 billion; (iii) Country-by-Country Report is required when the ultimate parent group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds VND 18 trillion. Taxpayers with total related-party transaction value below VND 30 billion, total revenue below VND 50 billion, and no transactions with parties resident in low-tax jurisdictions are exempt from the Local File requirement but must still file the TP disclosure form (Form 01/QL-DN a/k/a Phụ lục III) with the annual CIT finalization. All VAT-eligible and economically substantive transactions should be documented contemporaneously with the arm's length analysis; documentation must be prepared before the annual finalization and submitted to the tax authority within 30 days of a formal TP audit request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not adopt the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations licensing framework, but enforces a strict economic-substance doctrine through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Article 5 of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, Article 19 of the Tax Administration Law 38/2019, and the substance-over-form jurisprudence applied by Vietnamese courts. Tax authorities may disregard transactions, reclassify entities, and re-determine taxable income where intercompany arrangements lack genuine commercial rationale, have no real business purpose, or are designed principally to obtain tax or treaty benefits. A foreign-invested LLC engaging in video matching services must demonstrate: actual management and control in Vietnam, a physical office or demonstrable operational presence, resident employees performing material functions, real business risk assumption, ongoing revenue recognition in Vietnamese books, and a local bank account that receives and disburses commercial payments. Where the LLC is a mere nominal entity with decision-making and value creation outside Vietnam, the tax authority will treat the foreign principals as having a permanent establishment or recharacterize the purported expense deductions, deny treaty benefits under PPT, and apply withholding obligations with penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally recording only the net payout received from Apple IAP or Paymentwall while omitting app store gross proceeds; suppressing virtual gift, subscription, or advertising revenue; maintaining two sets of books; issuing or using fictitious invoices to inflate deductible expenses; structuring the video chat platform so that Vietnam-source revenue is booked in a foreign shell entity while the Vietnam LLC declares negligible income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative sanction of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax amount under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; late payment interest at 0.03% per day on the unpaid tax; full disallowance of fraudulent deductions; criminal prosecution under Article 200 of the Penal Code 2015 (amended 2017): for managing individuals, a fine from VND 100 million up to VND 4.5 billion and/or imprisonment from 6 months to 7 years depending on the scale of evasion; for the legal entity, fines up to VND 20 billion, suspension of the enterprise's operation for up to 2 years, or a permanent ban from the video telecommunications and app-ake business. The tax authority may also order public disclosure of the violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, CEO, and chief accountant bear personal criminal liability; Vietnamese courts routinely impose travel bans, exit-visa denial, and court-ordered asset freezes on directors while tax evasion investigations are pending. The corporate veil is pierced for the tax debt where the director has signed false declarations or caused the company's insolvency; directors may be ordered to make civil restitution of the full tax shortfall and, upon conviction, face imprisonment up to 7 years, plus a prohibition from holding managerial positions for 1 to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misdeclaration / Thin Capitalization / Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated intercompany licensing, brand, or content-moderation fees to the Vietnam LLC; paying an offshore parent a profit margin significantly outside the arm's length range for functions performed in Vietnam; executing circular transactions through low-tax jurisdictions to strip Vietnam-source profits; deducting interest on shareholder loans exceeding the 30% EBITDA thin-capitalization ratio under Article 16 of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP; failing to prepare or submit the required Local File, Master File, or TP disclosure form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may re-determine taxable income under the best-method rule, disregard contrived transactions, impose disallowed interest deductions above the 30% EBITDA ceiling, and adjust transfer prices to the median arm's length result. The additional assessed tax carries late-payment interest at 0.03% per day, plus an administrative penalty of up to 20% of the reassessed tax shortfall for under-declaration; failure to submit TP documentation is separately fined up to VND 20 million under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP. In severe cases, criminal tax evasion charges may be added when TP manipulation crosses the wilful-evasion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and chief accountants who sign false TP documentation are jointly and severally liable for the adjusted tax debt and face personal fines and imprisonment under Article 200 Penal Code; the General Department of Taxation may deny exit visas to the legal representative until the TP audit and settlement is complete; foreign shadow directors operating remotely without physical presence in Vietnam may be personally served through mutual legal assistance and barred from future entry to Vietnam until the liability is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Payment Aggregator Bypass / Unlicensed Payment Services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting funds through Apple IAP or Paymentwall as a facade to bypass Vietnam's payment-intermediary licensing requirements; facilitating anonymous in-app value transfers among users that can be monetized and withdrawn without customer due diligence; failing to report suspicious transactions involving virtual gift resale or conversion to cryptocurrency; intentionally concealing beneficial ownership of corporate bank accounts or layering payments through multiple shell accounts; conducting video match services with high-risk clients linked to fraud or human trafficking without AML/KYC controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under the Law on Anti-Money Laundering 2022 up to VND 200 million for legal entities that fail to perform customer identification, suspicious transaction reporting, or record keeping; the State Bank of Vietnam may suspend account operations and revoke related payment accreditations; immutative criminal liability under Article 324 of the Penal Code for money laundering applies to persons who transfer, convert, or conceal proceeds of crime, with imprisonment up to 15 years for individuals and fines up to VND 20 billion for legal entities; enterprise licenses may be revoked for recurrent violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are personally investigated in parallel with corporate sanctions; travel bans and exit denial are routinely imposed on signatories under AML emergency powers; personal assets may be seized and civilly confiscated as proceeds of crime; foreign investors found to have used nominee Vietnamese directors may be criminally charged and faces international arrest risk through INTERPOL notices, while the nominee directors face imprisonment for collusion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Vietnamese LLC with no physical office, no employees resident in Vietnam, no bank account, no substantive decision-making, and no actual service delivery while relying on the corporate form to claim CIT reversions, preferential rates, or DTA benefits; routing video chat revenue through a Hong Kong, Singapore, or Dubai conduit solely to obtain treaty withholding reductions; applying a 10% software incentive rate without software certification; failing to have the foreign shareholder provide a valid TRC; making year-end distributions without audited financials.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The GAAR forces re-determination of taxable income from substance over form, denies treaty benefits under the PPT/limitation-of-benefits provisions, reclassifies the company as a mere permanent establishment of the foreign operator, imposes FCT withholding at full domestic rates (10% CIT on royalties, 5% on interest, and 0% dividend WHT with full recharacterized income), and strips all preferential incentives. The taxpayer bears the burden of proving commercial substance; additional assessments carry 20% under-declaration penalties and 0.03% daily interest. The Ministry of Planning and Investment may also revoke the enterprise registration certificate for falsely declaring operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominee legal representative and the foreign shadow director are jointly and severally liable for the full reassessed tax and penalties; courts can pierce the corporate veil to seize personal bank accounts, freeze residential property, impose exit bans, and in serious cases pursue criminal fraud charges under Article 174 (fraudulent appropriation) or Article 200 Penal Code; the foreign beneficial owner who cannot be served in Vietnam may be subjected to mutual legal assistance, Interpol Red Notice issuance, and civil recognition of Vietnamese money judgments in the owner's home jurisdiction.
